title: Propeller pitch linkage joints, blade 1
description: The pitch linkage's joints and the kinematic dimensions between them, with no studies and almost no numbers: it exists to be BOUND to 3D geometry, so that the pitch-linkage solver can be handed nominal joint locations in the assembly frame. Nothing here should be quoted as a tolerance.

provenance.structure_source: Jeff, live, 2026-09-30, founding the `linkage` solver repo: the rigid bodies of the pitch linkage (base = hub + tangential-link mount + gas-spring mount; blade + pitch arm; pitch link assembly; pitch plate + piston; tangential link assembly), with the ask that this repo carry 'the right components' so that the 3D annotator can be used to select the spherical centres and the hub/gas-spring bores. The graph below is that statement of the mechanism; it is Jeff's description of his own design, not a reading of a drawing.
provenance.parts_source: The drawing numbers on every part below are read off parts lists extracted by drawing-checker runs, not transcribed from memory: 217755-001 A.1 PROPULSION ASSEMBLY (run 20260909_174538, sheet 1 parts list) for 212956-005 find 25 'PITCH ANTI ROTATION LINK ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER' qty 3, 215175-001 find 41 '...CW' qty 1 and 215175-002 find 73 '...CCW' qty '-'; 216231 B.1 HUB AND BLADE ASSEMBLY (run 20260904_184249) for 214373-002 find 1 'DUAL BEARING GEN5 HUB ASSEMBLY', 215071-001 find 11 'PITCH ARM, PROPELLER, CLOCKWISE', 216332-001 find 19 'BLADE BONDED ASSEMBLY' and 213862-002 find 30 'PITCH LINK ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER'; 213862-002 A (run 20260922_154236) for its own two rows, 213861-002 'PITCH LINK, PROPELLER' qty 1 and MS14101-3 qty 2. tolstack's dependency on drawing-checker is read-only (scripts/snapshot_drawing_checker.py).
provenance.configuration: The 217755-001 A.1 CW propulsion assembly as modelled at 72 degrees blade pitch -- the feather hard stop. That is the state the assembly STEP every installed mesh was extracted from is in, and the state the 3DX sweep sheet's own reference row (row 83, the row every actuator displacement in column K is measured from) describes.
provenance.no_worksheet: This document has no `provenance.worksheet`, deliberately: there is no structured read of a source workbook behind it, because there is no source workbook. Its one cited number comes from a 3DX sweep sheet in another repo, cited inline on the edge that carries it.
provenance.end_stop_travel_20261016: Handoff the_travel_between_the_end_stops_is_a_study, 2026-10-16. Structure and the two Jeff figures: forge note 20261016T144810_kk46rp. Face order and nominals: planes fitted with tolerance_stack/feature_geometry.py to the installed meshes asm217755_214699_002, asm217755_214698_002 and machined_213668; the worksheet records the Z values. The authored orientation of every edge in the end-stop chain is +Z at the feather stop, so a study walking it reads signs straight off the walk.
provenance.end_stop_travel_20261020: Handoff the_travel_chain_cites_its_three_drawings, 2026-10-20. Three drawings extracted by drawing-checker the same day (runs 20261020_134240_214698-002-A, 20261020_134300_214699-002-A, 20261020_134315_214958-002-A). Two terms cite them; the other two have no dimension on their drawing and stay mesh fits under a placeholder band, each saying so in its own source_ref. The stop surfaces were reconciled against Jeff's 72 deg section: the heads rest on the mount's end-stop surface and the cover's internal shoulder is the far stop, so two nodes were renamed (`piston_head_upper_top_face` to `piston_head_upper_step_face`, `gas_spring_mount_end_stop_face` to `piston_cover_end_stop_shoulder`; neither carried a binding) and the cover and mount edges are authored from the flange seat in +Z.
provenance.end_stop_travel_20261022: Handoff a_general_profile_note_bands_a_model_defined_term, 2026-10-22. The two terms with no dimension on their drawings are banded by each drawing's general profile note, on Jeff's ruling of 2026-10-20 (forge note 20261020T171900_km22z6): 214698-002 note 6 (profile 0.5, so ±0.25) and 213668-002 note 12 (profile 1, so ±0.5), each `drawing`/`traced` with the note as its anchor and the drawing's oversight said in its note. The assumed ±0.05 stand-ins are retired. 213668-002's 76.86 ±0.10 (datum A to the top face) is recorded as its own edge and not folded.

parts.name: propeller hub
parts.note: DUAL BEARING GEN5 HUB ASSEMBLY, 216231 B.1 find 1. The ground every load path returns to; it carries the spindle bore (the pitch system's expected CAD Z) and the blade root bearing bores (blade 1's expected CAD X). Installed 2026-10-01 by rotorkit's assembly_extract_20261001T022446Z and aliased the same day: `asm217755_214373_002`, 286 solids, the whole hub assembly.

parts.name: pitch arm
parts.note: PITCH ARM, PROPELLER, CLOCKWISE, 216231 B.1 find 11. The CCW hand is 215071-002 (find 47); this topology is the CW assembly. Installed 2026-10-01 and aliased: `asm217755_215071_001`, one solid, five instances -- one per blade.

parts.name: blade root
parts.note: BLADE BONDED ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, 216231 B.1 find 19 (the instrumented blade is 551438-001, find 2). `blade_oml` in data/meshes/ is a clean outer-mould-line export of the blade from a separate STEP, not this assembly -- it carries no root bearing geometry, so it is not aliased to this part. The real blade arrived 2026-10-01 as TWO geometries under this drawing number, and blade 1 carries the instrumented 551438-001 besides -- so this part still has no row, for a reason that is a decision rather than a missing file (see ISSUE_20260930_blade_1s_pitch_link_is_the_instrumented_546293_002.md).

parts.name: pitch link assembly
parts.note: PITCH LINK ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, 216231 B.1 find 30. Its own parts list (213862-002 A) is two rows: the body 213861-002 PITCH LINK, PROPELLER x1, and MS14101-3 x2. Blade 1's link is the instrumented variant, and this part's drawing number is the standard one: rotorkit's 2026-10-01 extraction shows the propeller carries five pitch links, with 546293-002 INSTRUMENTED PITCH LINK ASSEMBLY (216231 B.1 find 29) at instance 213862-002.1 and 213862-002 itself at .2 to .5. The two joint centres this document's `pitch_link_length` is about sit inside that .1 -- so the geometry is the instrumented link's, and the two agree with the 3DX sweep sheet's own nodes to under two microns, which is what says the kinematics are the same link. Which drawing this part should carry is a decision nobody has made: ISSUE_20260930_blade_1s_pitch_link_is_the_instrumented_546293_002.md.

parts.name: pitch-link spherical bearing
parts.note: MS14101-3, self-lubricated self-aligning spherical bearing, narrow (AS81820) -- 213862-002 A's parts list, qty 2. The pitch link's two joint centres ARE the two ball centres of this part's two instances, which is why it is a part here and not a note. This is the one part of this linkage with an installed mesh today: `asm217755_MS14101_3_815597cb`, whose two instances sit at 213862-002.1/MS14101-3.1 and .2 -- that being blade 1's INSTRUMENTED link, see this document's `pitch_link` part. rotorkit's 2026-10-01 run re-extracted the same solid under a second geometry signature (`asm217755_MS14101_3_1ec77e91`, same assembly, same label, same placements), which briefly gave the store two directories for one solid -- resolved 2026-10-01 (handoff mesh_store_reconciled_to_the_pure_signature): both signatures moved to the pure-key value `815597cb` under shape_signature_is_pure, confirming they were always one solid, so the two directories fused into this one and the old `1ec77e91` copy moved to `data/meshes_superseded/`. ISSUE_20260930_one_solid_two_geometry_signatures_across_two_runs.md carries the history.

parts.name: 215177-001 pitch plate
parts.note: PITCH PLATE ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW, 217755-001 A.1 find 32. The same physical part topology_pitch_system.json names; the id is reused so the declared alias table keeps resolving it to the installed mesh. That mesh is the INSTALLATION (plate plus its nine NAS77 bushings, 10 solids); its one machined detail is installed separately as `asm217755_215735_001`.

parts.name: gas spring
parts.note: PMF200521, a two-solid vendor item (body + rod) occurring three times inside 215176-002 in the assembly STEP. Note what the 217755-001 A.1 parts list does NOT carry: any gas-spring row at all. That release carries a HYDRAULIC BRAKE ASSEMBLY (217676-001, find 85) instead, so the gas spring in the STEP is the earlier configuration, which is the one this linkage describes.

parts.name: 214700-002 gas-spring piston body
parts.note: PISTON BODY, GAS SPRING, PROPELLER, 217755-001 find 88 (docs/tolerance_stacks/WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md, the find-number table; drawing 214700-002-A read there). Rigidly bolted to the pitch plate -- Jeff, 2026-10-14: "it's rigidly bolted to the piston and it has the cylindrical surface that rides on the gas spring linear guides" -- so it rides the `pitch_plate` body in a linkage run (linkage names it there from run P2 on). In the assembly STEP it is the occurrence `P3-214700.3`, whose bolts (`NAS6403U13H`) are installed. The piston body is installed too (rotorkit's `extract_the_gas_spring_piston`, run assembly_extract_20261015T012912Z, one solid, one instance) and `part_mesh_aliases.json` carries its row.

parts.name: 213668-002 gas-spring mount
parts.note: The same physical part topology_pitch_system.json names; id reused so the alias table keeps resolving it to `machined_213668`.

parts.name: 215175-002 tangential link mount
parts.note: The same id topology_pitch_system.json declares, reused. Read the alias table's row for it before assuming which hand is on screen: 217755-001 A.1's parts list carries BOTH dash numbers -- find 41, 215175-001 '...CW', qty 1, and find 73, 215175-002 '...CCW', qty '-' -- so the CW assembly every installed mesh came from contains the -001.

parts.name: 212956-005 pitch anti-rotation link assembly
parts.note: PITCH ANTI ROTATION LINK ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, 217755-001 A.1 find 25, qty 3 -- the TANGENTIAL (anti-rotation) link, not the pitch link. A 2026-09-14 rotorkit lesson guessed `pitch_link -> 212956-005`; the parts list refutes it and 216231 B.1 find 30 names 213862-002 as the pitch link assembly. The mesh `asm217755_212956_005` is four solids: the link body, an MS14101-3, an MS14103-3 and a bolt.

parts.name: tangential-link bearing, narrow end
parts.note: MS14101-3, the narrow spherical bearing at the tangential link's mount end. Installed as `asm217755_MS14101_3_34f032f0` -- a DIFFERENT solid from the pitch link's `_815597cb`, both named MS14101-3 in the STEP, which is why the mesh store suffixes the geometry signature.

parts.name: tangential-link bearing, wide end
parts.note: MS14103-3, the wide spherical bearing at the tangential link's other end: same .1900 in bore as MS14101-3, wider body (docs/spec_library, event 0006, RBC Aerospace plain bearings pp. 21-22). Installed as `asm217755_MS14103_3`, three instances, one per tangential link.

parts.name: 214699-002 lower piston head
parts.note: Jeff's forge note 20261016T144810_kk46rp names it (lower piston head 214699-002). Installed as `asm217755_214699_002` (10 faces, one solid, rotorkit run assembly_extract_20261015T012912Z). Its drawing is in no inbox as of 2026-10-16, so every number on it is a mesh fit. Its lower face carries a FLATNESS callout only (Jeff) -- a form tolerance with no length, recorded on the node, not as an edge.

parts.name: 214698-002 upper piston head
parts.note: Jeff's forge note 20261016T144810_kk46rp names it (upper piston head 214698-002). Installed as `asm217755_214698_002` (161 faces, one solid, same rotorkit run). Its drawing, 214698-002 A, arrived 2026-10-20 and dimensions none of the stop chain's faces; the step height is a mesh-fit nominal banded by the drawing's general profile note 6 (2026-10-22).

parts.name: 214958-002 piston cover
parts.note: Named by Jeff in forge note 20261016T144810_kk46rp (piston cover 214958-002; length from bottom flange to end stop surface ~82.154 mm). NO installed mesh and no drawing in any inbox as of 2026-10-16 (checked drawing-checker and tolstack drawings inboxes), so the one number on it is Jeff's, cited as such, and the annotator's 'no installed mesh' empty state is the honest answer for it. It sits in the main rigid body with the tan link mount 215175-001 and the gas-spring mount.

nodes.name: hub spindle bore axis -- the gas-spring bushing bore
nodes.note: Expected to be the CAD Z axis, and expected is the word: nothing in this repo states it, which is exactly why this node exists to be bound. Jeff, 2026-09-30: 'Might as well also select the hub/gas spring bores even though I'm fairly confident they're aligned with z and x axes.'

nodes.name: hub blade-1 root bearing bore
nodes.note: Expected to be the CAD X axis for blade 1, on the same evidence (none) as the spindle bore above.

nodes.name: pitch arm root clamp face against the blade root
nodes.note: Where the pitch arm is clamped to the blade root, and therefore the arm's own end of the blade pitch axis.

nodes.name: pitch arm pitch-link attachment bore
nodes.note: The lug bore the pitch link's lower joint bolt passes through. One part, not two: the bolt that makes it a mate is not a part of this topology.

nodes.name: pitch link lower spherical-bearing centre
nodes.note: The ball centre of the MS14101-3 at 213862-002.1/MS14101-3.1. On the LINK rather than on the bearing because the two joint centres are two instances of one bearing part, and a topology part id names a part, not an instance: a node on `spherical_bearing_pitch_link` could not tell the two apart. The geometry to bind is on that bearing's mesh all the same.

nodes.name: pitch link upper spherical-bearing centre
nodes.note: The ball centre of the MS14101-3 at 213862-002.1/MS14101-3.2 -- the pitch-plate end. Same instance-versus-part reasoning as the lower centre.

nodes.name: pitch-link bearing outer-race OD
nodes.note: The press fit that holds the bearing in the link's housing bore. Carried as a feature of the BEARING alone: it is a mating surface in the joint, but no edge in this document is a dimension of the pitch link across it, and a part named on an interface that no incident edge uses is an authoring error the viewer reports rather than draws.

nodes.name: MS14101-3 ball centre
nodes.note: The piece part's own spherical centre, as distinct from either joint centre above: one part, one centre, two instances of it in the assembly.

nodes.name: MS14101-3 ball bore
nodes.note: The .1900 in bore through the ball, which the joint bolt passes through. Bore B 4.826 mm, -0.013 (docs/spec_library event 0006, RBC Aerospace plain bearings p. 21) -- cited here as context for a reader, not as this node's value; a node carries no value.

nodes.name: pitch plate spindle bore axis
nodes.note: The plate's own central bore, expected coaxial with the hub spindle bore and with CAD Z. Expected, again, is the word.

nodes.name: tangential link mount-end spherical-bearing centre
nodes.note: Phase 2. The MS14101-3 ball centre at this end of 212956-005.

nodes.name: tangential link plate-end spherical-bearing centre
nodes.note: Phase 2. The MS14103-3 ball centre at this end of 212956-005.

nodes.name: MS14101-3 outer-race OD
nodes.note: Phase 2. A feature of the bearing alone, for the reason the pitch-link seat's note gives.

nodes.name: MS14103-3 outer-race OD
nodes.note: Phase 2. A feature of the bearing alone, for the reason the pitch-link seat's note gives.

nodes.name: gas-spring mount base face against the hub
nodes.note: Where 213668-002 bolts to the hub, and therefore the mount's own datum.

nodes.name: tangential link mount base face against the hub
nodes.note: Phase 2. Where 215175-001 bolts to the hub.

nodes.name: lower piston head lower face on the gas-spring mount's end-stop surface -- the main datum
nodes.note: The feather (72 deg) hard stop and the datum of the end-stop analysis: the lower head's lower face resting on the mount's end-stop surface. Settled 2026-10-20 against Jeff's section of the gas spring at 72 deg (docs/sessions/shots_20261020_strategy_stop_face/): the head stack sits at the bottom, on the mount's face, and the gap that is the travel is ABOVE the heads, up to the cover's internal shoulder. Until then this node read 'against the cover end stop'; the cover owns the other stop, not this one. 214699-002 A gives this face a flatness callout (0.05) and a parallelism callout, and no length. On the mesh, face 7 of `asm217755_214699_002` (normal -Z, z 234.169 in the part frame) is a plain plane: fit residual 0. The mount side is face 1080 of `machined_213668`.

nodes.name: lower piston head upper face against the upper head lower face
nodes.note: The two heads seat against each other, not at the two ends of the piston body: face 0 of the lower head (+Z, z 236.660) and face 113 of the upper head (-Z, z 236.6596) are one plane to 0.0004 mm in the assembly frame. That is what decided `piston_body_between_heads` is NOT a member of the chain.

nodes.name: upper piston head step face -- the extend stop's moving side
nodes.note: The step face at part-frame Z 243.216 (face 110 of `asm217755_214698_002`, +Z, assembly Z 219.882), named by Jeff 2026-10-20: highlighted on the head in its own frame and measured in his CAD section at 72 deg pitch, 64.465 mm to the cover's internal shoulder (Jeff corrected that to 64.440 the same day: his CATIA kinematic model has a 0.025 mm interference at the 72 deg rest and is coincident at -7 deg) (docs/sessions/shots_20261020_strategy_stop_face/). It is a node of its own, not one with `piston_cover_end_stop_shoulder`, because a hard contact is one node and this study measures the clearance. The head's other +Z planes (240.669, 245.375, 249.169) are not the stop. 214698-002 A does not dimension this face's height; the drawing defers to the model (note 5), so the height is a mesh fit, banded since 2026-10-22 by the drawing's general profile note 6.

nodes.name: piston cover bottom flange against the mount flange
nodes.note: Where the cover is clamped to the mount. Both end-stop surfaces are measured from this plane, which is why it is the pivot of the chain.

nodes.name: piston cover internal end-stop shoulder -- the extend stop
nodes.note: The cover's internal shoulder: the surface the upper head's step face meets at the extend stop, 82.154 mm in from the cover's bottom flange face (214958-002 A sheet 3, SECTION CUT A-A). Until 2026-10-20 this node was named for the mount's end-stop surface; the section view shows that surface is where the heads rest at 72 deg (node `endstop_feather_contact`), and the shoulder is the cover's. No mesh of the cover exists.

edges.name: pitch link length between spherical-bearing centres

dimension.name: pitch link length, lower bearing centre to upper bearing centre

source_ref.note:
The distance between the sheet's own two node columns at 72 degrees blade pitch (row 83, the row its column K measures every actuator displacement from): Pitch Arm Node C83:E83 = (83.000, -44.550, -22.700), Pitch Plate Node G83:I83 = (84.972, -17.139, 79.666), |A - P| = 105.9908 mm. It is a rigid link, so the length must come out constant over the sweep, and it does -- over all 80 rows (blade pitch -7 to +72, rows 4 to 83) it ranges 105.9896 to 105.9915, a spread of 0.0019 mm, which is the sheet's own three-decimal rounding and not a tolerance.
`untraced`, and the arithmetic is why it is not better rather than why it is: the subtraction and the norm settle `traced` against `inferred` -- the sheet states the endpoints and not the length -- and say nothing about the SUPPORT, which is this workbook and no second document. The SOP's rule is that a value whose only support is 'the source workbook says so' is `untraced` and goes on the gap list however reasonable it looks, and this edge does. What would move it: 213861-002's own drawing, which this repo has not acquired. This handoff's own fit of the two bearing centres agrees to 0.00023 mm and is deliberately NOT leaned on -- a fit is a measurement of a mesh, not a citation.
DIVERGENCE RESOLVED 2026-10-01, in this value's favour: docs/topologies/topology_pitch_system.json's own `pitch_link_length` edge stated 109.4 mm for the same hole-to-hole distance on this same link -- from a different workbook (260825_End_Stop_JC.xlsx K3) and carried in that edge's `properties` rather than in a `dimension`, which is why nothing paired the two. 3.41 mm apart, and a rigid link's length does not change with pitch. That document was corrected to 105.9908 mm; see its edge's citation note for the full argument, and ISSUE_20260930_two_topologies_state_the_pitch_link_length_3mm_apart.md. tests/test_tolerance_stack.py::test_one_part_and_feature_states_one_nominal_in_every_topology_that_states_it now pairs the two and goes red if they part again. Resolved does not mean verified: this value is still `untraced` for the reason above, and 213861-002's drawing is still what would move it.
The workbook lives in another repo, read-only: C:\workspace\atp-post\docs\references\250530_pitch_motion_ratios.xlsx.
source_ref.callout: Pitch Arm Node / Pitch Plate Node, X Y Z

dimension.note: min == max because the sheet carries a nominal and NO tolerance -- so this edge appears on the gap list twice over: as a value with no band recorded, and as an unverified value, which workbook-only support makes it. A pitch-link length tolerance would come from 213861-002's own drawing.

edges.name: MS14101-3 ball centre offset from its outer-race seat
edges.note: No value recorded. Nominally zero by the bearing's own construction -- a self-aligning spherical bearing's ball swivels about the centre of its race -- but no document in this repo states it, so this edge carries no dimension rather than an invented zero. What would close it: MS14101's own concentricity callout in the RBC catalog (pp. 21-22, not read for this), or this handoff's fit of the two spherical faces of `asm217755_MS14101_3_815597cb`.

edges.name: MS14101-3 ball bore axis to ball centre
edges.note: No value recorded. The pair of features Jeff binds first, because both are on the one mesh of this linkage that is installed today: the ball (a spherical face) and the bore (a cylindrical one). What would close it: the same two sources as the sibling edge above.

edges.name: pitch arm radius, blade root clamp face to link bore
edges.note: No value recorded. The lever arm that turns the pitch link's travel into blade pitch, and the quantity the solver most wants a number for. What would close it: 215071-001's own drawing, which this repo has not acquired, or a fit of the arm's mesh once rotorkit installs it. The 3DX sweep sheet does NOT give it -- the sheet's Pitch Arm Node is the joint centre, and the blade axis is not in it.

edges.name: blade root bearing bore to pitch arm clamp face
edges.note: No value recorded. What would close it: 216332-001's own drawing. This edge is what makes the blade pitch axis and the pitch arm one chain rather than two components.

edges.name: hub spindle axis to blade-1 root bearing axis offset
edges.note: No value recorded. Expected to be zero -- the two axes are expected to intersect, Z and X -- and a zero written here on that expectation would be exactly the invented nominal this repo refuses. What would close it: 214373-002's own drawing, or a fit of the hub's two bores once rotorkit installs its mesh.

edges.name: pitch plate spindle axis to pitch-link attachment bore, radius
edges.note: No value recorded. Radius and height (the sibling edge) are the two components of one offset, carried as two edges because a solver wants them separately. What would close it: 215177-001 or 215735-001's drawing, or a fit of the installed `asm217755_215177_001` mesh -- whose spindle bore and link bores are both there to be bound today.

edges.name: pitch plate spindle axis to pitch-link attachment bore, height
edges.note: No value recorded. The axial component of the same offset the radius edge carries -- a second edge between the same two interfaces, deliberately, because the two components answer two different questions and a single scalar would answer neither.

edges.name: pitch plate spindle axis to gas-spring attachment bore
edges.note: No value recorded. What would close it: 215177-001's drawing, or a fit of the installed mesh.

edges.name: pitch plate spindle axis to tangential-link attachment bore
edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2. What would close it: 215177-001's drawing, or a fit of the installed mesh.

edges.name: gas spring mount bushing bore to rod-end bore
edges.note: No value recorded, and it is a function of stroke rather than a fixed length: what a solver wants here is the installed length AT 72 degrees, which is the state the assembly STEP is in. What would close it: a PMF200521 vendor datasheet (none in data/inbox/specs/ as of 2026-09-30), or a fit of the installed `asm217755_PMF200521` mesh's two end bores.

edges.name: pitch arm link bore to pitch link lower bearing centre
edges.note: No value recorded. The lower joint's own closure: the ball centre sits on the arm bore's axis, and by how much it does not is the joint's play. What would close it: the bearing's and the lug's own fits, plus a clearance from 215071-001's drawing.

edges.name: pitch plate link bore to pitch link upper bearing centre
edges.note: No value recorded. The upper joint's own closure, the mirror of the lower one.

edges.name: hub spindle bore axis to pitch plate spindle bore axis
edges.note: No value recorded. The plate rides on the spindle, so these two axes are expected coaxial; how far from coaxial they are allowed to be is a drawing question nobody has answered here.

edges.name: hub spindle bore axis to gas-spring mount bushing bore
edges.note: No value recorded. The hub's spindle bore IS the gas-spring bushing bore in Jeff's statement of the mechanism; this edge is where the two are compared once both are bound, and it is the reason the hub node is named for both.

edges.note: No value recorded.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2. The tangential link's analogue of `pitch_link_length`, and unlike that edge the 3DX sweep sheet does not carry its endpoints. What would close it: 213863-004's drawing (acquired 2026-09-10, run 20260910_154233), or a fit of the installed `asm217755_212956_005` mesh, whose four solids include both bearings.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2.

edges.note: No value recorded. edges.note: No value recorded. What would close it: 214373-002's own drawing. topology_pitch_system.json carries this quantity under `gas_spring_mount_position`, with a drawing citation that is still `untraced` (its 2026-09-06 retrace) -- read that edge before re-tracing this one, and do not copy its band across: the two documents do not measure between the same pair of interfaces.

edges.note: No value recorded. Phase 2. What would close it: 215198 sheet 1, whose `79.00 +/-0.10` was traced on 2026-09-10 and is the mount detail's own height -- but check the endpoints before copying it, because this edge is between THIS document's two interfaces and that trace was read for a different document's.

edges.name: hub spindle bore axis to tangential link mount seat

notes: Studyless by design. This topology has no studies and is not an analysis. It is a map of the pitch linkage's joints built to be bound to 3D geometry in apps/annotate/, so that scripts/fit_bound_features.py can hand the `linkage` solver nominal joint locations in the assembly frame at 72 degrees. Summing anything here would be summing a document that deliberately holds almost no numbers.

The only edge that carries a value is `pitch_link_length`, derived from the 3DX sweep sheet's own two node columns and cited cell-for-cell -- and cited `untraced`, because the only support is that workbook. The derivation settles `traced` against `inferred`; it says nothing about whether a second document stands behind the number, and the SOP's rule is that workbook-only support is `untraced` and goes on the gap list however reasonable it looks. Every other edge carries no dimension at all. That is this repo's cite-or-gap rule applied honestly to a document whose numbers have not been acquired: an `untraced` band of 0.000 would put a plausible number on a reader's screen, and a reader cannot tell a placeholder zero from a measured one. Each valueless edge's own `note` says in one line what would close it -- a named drawing, or a fit of a named mesh.

A consequence worth knowing: the DAG page's gap list reports an edge whose dimension is *unverified*, not an edge that has no dimension at all (scripts/build_topology_projection.py, `topology_gaps`), because a valueless edge there has always meant 'the quantity a study computes'. So this document's gaps are visible on its edges, each rendered as a value with no source, and only `pitch_link_length` reaches the gap list -- as a value with no tolerance band recorded, which it is. Filed as ISSUE_20260930_a_valueless_structural_edge_is_invisible_to_the_gap_list.md.

What has a mesh today, which is what decides what Jeff can bind: the pitch-link bearing (`spherical_bearing_pitch_link`), the pitch plate (`pitch_plate_215177_001`), the gas spring (`gas_spring`), the gas-spring mount (`gas_spring_mount_213668_002`), the tangential link mount (`tan_link_mount_215175_002`), the whole tangential link (`tan_link_212956_005` and its two bearings), and -- since rotorkit's 2026-10-01 extraction -- the `hub` and the `pitch_arm`. Still without a row: `pitch_link`'s body and `blade_root`, whose meshes ARE installed but whose identity is open, because blade 1 carries the instrumented variants of both. The annotator's 'no installed mesh' empty state is the honest answer for those two until that is decided.

The two pitch-link joint centres are nodes of the link, not of the bearing, because they are two instances of one bearing part and a topology part id names a part. The bearing carries its own features instead -- its ball centre against its seat and against its bore -- and a `gap` edge from that ball centre to each of the link's two joint centres says which geometry a reader binds for each. Those gap edges are nominally zero and carry no value; what they carry is the identity.

Update 2026-10-16 (handoff the_travel_between_the_end_stops_is_a_study): the first study over this graph now exists, `study_vpa_pitch_linkage_travel_between_end_stops.json`, and the 'studyless by design' note above is no longer true of this document as a whole. The mechanism joints above are still a map to bind and still hold almost no numbers; the end-stop chain added today is a separate small piece that does carry them, each term cited to its part drawing: two to a dimension (since 2026-10-20) and two to the drawing's general profile note (since 2026-10-22), listed in docs/tolerance_stacks/WORKSHEET_gas_spring_end_stop_travel.md.
